questions.question: Name the following compounds: NaCl, CaS, CO, SO2 and CaCO3.
questions.expected_answer: NaCl: sodium chloride. CaS: calcium sulfide. CO: carbon monoxide. SO2: sulfur dioxide. CaCO3: calcium carbonate.

questions.question: Write the formulas for carbon dioxide, sulfur trioxide, dinitrogen monoxide and magnesium oxide.
questions.expected_answer: Carbon dioxide: CO2. Sulfur trioxide: SO3. Dinitrogen monoxide: N2O. Magnesium oxide: MgO.

questions.question: Explain why prefixes are used when naming CO and CO2 but not when naming MgO, and state what the ending -ate indicates.
questions.expected_answer: Carbon and oxygen are both non-metals and can combine in more than one ratio, so prefixes (mono, di) are needed to show the number of oxygen atoms and to distinguish the two different compounds. Magnesium and oxygen (a metal and a non-metal) combine in only one ratio, so no prefix is needed. The ending -ate indicates that the compound contains a group in which a non-metal is combined with oxygen, e.g. carbonate (CO3) or sulfate (SO4).
